title: Electromagnetism
overview: This unit covers the fundamental properties of electromagnetic waves, the dual wave-particle nature of light, electric charges, and electric forces. These concepts form the foundation for understanding electromagnetic induction and circuits in Unit 9.

concepts: Light exhibits both wave and particle properties
Photons are the particle aspect of electromagnetic radiation
Electromagnetic waves consist of oscillating electric and magnetic fields
Energy is quantized at the quantum level
De Broglie wavelength relates particle momentum to wave properties
Double-slit experiment demonstrates wave behavior of particles
Electric charge is a fundamental property of matter
Like charges repel, unlike charges attract
Charge is conserved in isolated systems
Coulomb's Law describes the force between charged particles
Electric forces act along the line connecting charges
Principle of superposition applies to electric forces and fields
Conductors vs. insulators in charge distribution
Electric field represents the force per unit charge in a region
Electric field lines point from positive to negative charges
Field strength decreases with squared distance
Charged particles experience force in electric fields
Electric fields can do work on charged particles

Force on a Charge in an Electric Field

connections_to_unit9: Electric fields lead to the concept of electric potential (voltage)
Understanding of charges and fields is fundamental to analyzing circuits
Electromagnetic waves are generated by changing electric and magnetic fields
Magnetic fields are produced by moving charges (electric currents)
Changing magnetic fields induce electric fields (electromagnetic induction)
Energy transformations in electromagnetic systems apply to circuit analysis

laboratory_activities.title: Photoelectric Effect Simulation
laboratory_activities.description: Students use PhET simulations to investigate the relationship between light frequency, intensity, and electron ejection, helping them understand the particle nature of light and the concept of photon energy.

laboratory_activities.title: Double-Slit Experiment
laboratory_activities.description: Students perform the classic double-slit experiment with light and analyze interference patterns, then compare with simulations of electron diffraction patterns to visualize wave-particle duality.

laboratory_activities.title: Electric Fields and Forces
laboratory_activities.description: Students map electric field lines using various charge configurations and measure forces between charged objects, connecting the concept of fields to observable forces.

laboratory_activities.title: Electromagnetic Energy and Resonance
laboratory_activities.description: Students investigate resonant absorption of EM waves in different materials and connect this to the concept of energy transfer in wave systems.
